description:
Ship Capture v3.0.3

Hack unmanned ships. Board manned ships. Every captured ship joins your fleet after the battle.

Game version:

0.98a-RC8

Requires:

LunaLib

(required only for the in-game Mod Settings UI; without it the mod runs on the defaults in data/config/modSettings.json)

Download:

Source code:

What is this?

A standalone mod that lets you take enemy ships in battle through two separate mechanics: hacking for unmanned ships and boarding for manned ships. Captured ships join your fleet after the battle, and the battle report, bounties and fleet composition are all handled correctly.

Note: English is not my native language. This post was translated and lightly edited with the help of AI; please excuse any awkward phrasing.

Compatibility with ongoing saves:

Adding to an ongoing game: Safe (verified) - the mod only adds two hullmods and three fighter wings, no world content. Verified in an ongoing save.Updating: Initial release - no older versions to update from.Removing from an ongoing game: Not safe - captured ships carry this mod's hullmods and fighter wings in their variants; deleting the mod from a save that used it can break that save on load. Start a new game instead. (A safe-removal helper was attempted but did not work reliably in testing; a working solution may come in a future version.)

Warning: The values and their effects in this mod may disrupt game balance. It is strongly recommended to adjust them to your preferred levels first in the Mod Settings. When using this mod, make sure to exit the fleet command window (TAB or ESC) promptly after entering combat. You must enter a battle map at least once before you can freely continue fighting either in the command window or on the battle map. Otherwise, a bug may occur: ships with full capture counters will skip the transition period and instantly join the player's faction.

Features

Hacking Array (hullmod) - locks onto an enemy unmanned ship (Remnant automated ships, drone ships) and hacks it over time until control is seized.
Each equipped ship locks one target in range (prefers the target with the highest progress; multiple arrays on the same target combine: final effect = base x 2^(n/(n+1))).If the target leaves range, hacking pauses and the accumulated progress is kept; it re-locks another target if available, otherwise waits for the original.At 100% progress the target is paralyzed (5 s by default), switches to your side and joins your fleet after the battle.A successful capture spreads progress to other hackable ships within 2000 range and triggers a hack cooldown shared by the arrays that locked the target.Boarding Pod (fighter wing, Light / Medium / Heavy) - bomber-type fighters that assault enemy manned ships and accumulate boarding hits until control is seized.
Only fighters with CR above 0 can score a hit: touching the target within the touch range (120 for a frigate, scaling up with hull size) counts one hit; a successful hit zeroes the fighter's ammo and CR, so it must return to its carrier to resupply before boarding again.Hits required by hull size (defaults): frigate 25 / destroyer 38 / cruiser 63 / capital 100.Wing contacts add progress at different rates: Light x1 / Medium x2 / Heavy x5 per successful touch.Fighters prioritize your locked target (the R key) within max engagement range (4000 by default).Purchaseable at military markets (generic_military).Boarding Driver Core (hullmod, 0 OP) - drives the electronic-interference malfunction rolls for the boarding side (works with the Boarding Pod wings).
Once boarding progress passes 40%, a malfunction check runs every 10 s: chance = 20% + (progress - 40%) x 1% (40% -> 20%, 50% -> 30%, 70% -> 50%, 100% -> 80%).On success, one random malfunction triggers: engines flame out (cannot move) / weapons lock (cannot fire) / shields fail (cannot raise).Above 70% progress a critical malfunction can trigger (longer duration + small hull loss).Sunk-ship retaliation - when a ship with accumulated boarding hits is destroyed, one-shot boarding fighters are released at its wreck to continue the fight (set the sunk-return fraction to 0 to disable).Progress display - boarding/hack progress is shown as floating text above the target. (A colored-arc mode was experimental and is not reliably working in this version; it defaults to OFF and is not recommended.)Capture blacklist - add ship hull ids, one per line, to capture_blacklist.txt in the mod root to exclude them from hacking and boarding.Battle-end backstop - if the enemy has no surviving deployed ships for 10 seconds, the enemy fleet is ordered to retreat so battles always end cleanly.Capture transition - captured targets go through a short paralyzed, phase-like transition (board 10 s / hack 5 s, follows battle speed), then switch to your side; after capture they slowly repair (+0.5% max hull per second, up to 20% total).Post-battle ownership - captured ships join your fleet directly after the battle (captain removed; counted as your kills for bounty settlements).

Showcase

Screenshots



Omega Hackable

Detailed mechanics and settings
Mod Settings (LunaLib)
Almost every value is adjustable in-game via Mod Settings: hack range/rate, ECM multipliers, size multipliers, boarding hit requirements, malfunction chances and durations, transition times, repair rate, enemy-can-use toggle, custom fighter sprite toggle and more. A linked-slider scheme keeps the settings page compact: only the frigate-tier values are exposed, and the other hull sizes derive automatically.

Compatibility and known issues
Made for 0.98a-RC8; not tested against other versions.The mod was developed and tested in a partially Chinese-localized environment; behavior in a full English environment is not yet fully confirmed (feedback welcome).Known limitation: captures completed while the battle stays in fleet-control (strategy) mode the whole time may skip the transition animation (final ownership is unaffected); it recovers after entering combat mode once.Ship hulls added by other mods work as capture targets unless blacklisted.
FAQ
Q 
Why does nothing happen when I board? 
A 
Boarding hits require fighters with CR above 0 to touch the target; install the Boarding Driver Core (0 OP) on at least one of your ships if you want the malfunction effects. 
Q 
Why is my captured ship missing after battle? 
A 
Captured ships join your fleet directly after the battle ends; check the Reserve tab of your fleet. Ships still in their transition phase when the battle ends are also handled by the backstop. 
Q 
Can enemies use this mod against me? 
A 
By default yes (toggle in Mod Settings, "enemy can use"): enemy Hacking Arrays and Boarding Pods work from the enemy perspective. Turn it off if you do not want enemies to capture your ships. 
Q 
How do I exclude a ship from capture? 
A 
Add its hull id to capture_blacklist.txt in the mod root. 
Q 
Compressed file download was just loose files once unzipped? 
A 
Create a folder with the same name as the compressed file inside the mods folder, and extract the contents of the compressed file into that folder.

AI use disclaimer
Some or all assets and code in this mod were created using AI tools:
Code: Doubao (ByteDance's AI assistant) - the entire Java codebase was written by the AI, referencing vanilla Starsector code and the open-source mods listed in Credits below, then tested and iterated in-game.Fighter sprites: Doubao (AI-generated pixel art), with hand-drawn adjustments by the author.The author is a complete coding novice and this is their first mod; the AI did not use any additional training data beyond its base model. The mod was tested and verified in-game across many iterations before release.

Credits and permissions

Ship and Weapon Pack (DarkRevenant)Iron Shell (Techpriest & Selkie & Avanitia)Superweapons Arsenal 3.0 (Mira / KindaStrange / mllhild)Boarding Attack (zouyx)LunaLib (Lukas04)Permissions: the mod may be freely reposted and further developed. If any asset infringes on your work, please report it and it will be removed immediately.

Feedback and bug reports are welcome!

For bugs, please include your game and mod versions, enabled mods and steps to reproduce. A relevant log or screenshot helps a lot.

Ship Capture v3.0.3
Hack unmanned ships. Board manned ships. Every captured ship joins your fleet after the battle.

Game version: 0.98a-RC8
Requires: LunaLib (required only for the in-game Mod Settings UI; without it the mod runs on the defaults in data/config/modSettings.json)

Download:
Source code:

What is this?

A standalone mod that lets you take enemy ships in battle through two separate mechanics: hacking for unmanned ships and boarding for manned ships. Captured ships join your fleet after the battle, and the battle report, bounties and fleet composition are all handled correctly.

Note: English is not my native language. This post was translated and lightly edited with the help of AI; please excuse any awkward phrasing.

Compatibility with ongoing saves:
  • Adding to an ongoing game: Safe (verified) - the mod only adds two hullmods and three fighter wings, no world content. Verified in an ongoing save.
  • Updating: Initial release - no older versions to update from.
  • Removing from an ongoing game: Not safe - captured ships carry this mod's hullmods and fighter wings in their variants; deleting the mod from a save that used it can break that save on load. Start a new game instead. (A safe-removal helper was attempted but did not work reliably in testing; a working solution may come in a future version.)
Warning: The values and their effects in this mod may disrupt game balance. It is strongly recommended to adjust them to your preferred levels first in the Mod Settings. When using this mod, make sure to exit the fleet command window (TAB or ESC) promptly after entering combat. You must enter a battle map at least once before you can freely continue fighting either in the command window or on the battle map. Otherwise, a bug may occur: ships with full capture counters will skip the transition period and instantly join the player's faction.

Features

  • Hacking Array (hullmod) - locks onto an enemy unmanned ship (Remnant automated ships, drone ships) and hacks it over time until control is seized.
    • Each equipped ship locks one target in range (prefers the target with the highest progress; multiple arrays on the same target combine: final effect = base x 2^(n/(n+1))).
    • If the target leaves range, hacking pauses and the accumulated progress is kept; it re-locks another target if available, otherwise waits for the original.
    • At 100% progress the target is paralyzed (5 s by default), switches to your side and joins your fleet after the battle.
    • A successful capture spreads progress to other hackable ships within 2000 range and triggers a hack cooldown shared by the arrays that locked the target.
  • Boarding Pod (fighter wing, Light / Medium / Heavy) - bomber-type fighters that assault enemy manned ships and accumulate boarding hits until control is seized.
    • Only fighters with CR above 0 can score a hit: touching the target within the touch range (120 for a frigate, scaling up with hull size) counts one hit; a successful hit zeroes the fighter's ammo and CR, so it must return to its carrier to resupply before boarding again.
    • Hits required by hull size (defaults): frigate 25 / destroyer 38 / cruiser 63 / capital 100.
    • Wing contacts add progress at different rates: Light x1 / Medium x2 / Heavy x5 per successful touch.
    • Fighters prioritize your locked target (the R key) within max engagement range (4000 by default).
    • Purchaseable at military markets (generic_military).
  • Boarding Driver Core (hullmod, 0 OP) - drives the electronic-interference malfunction rolls for the boarding side (works with the Boarding Pod wings).
    • Once boarding progress passes 40%, a malfunction check runs every 10 s: chance = 20% + (progress - 40%) x 1% (40% -> 20%, 50% -> 30%, 70% -> 50%, 100% -> 80%).
    • On success, one random malfunction triggers: engines flame out (cannot move) / weapons lock (cannot fire) / shields fail (cannot raise).
    • Above 70% progress a critical malfunction can trigger (longer duration + small hull loss).
  • Sunk-ship retaliation - when a ship with accumulated boarding hits is destroyed, one-shot boarding fighters are released at its wreck to continue the fight (set the sunk-return fraction to 0 to disable).
  • Progress display - boarding/hack progress is shown as floating text above the target. (A colored-arc mode was experimental and is not reliably working in this version; it defaults to OFF and is not recommended.)
  • Capture blacklist - add ship hull ids, one per line, to capture_blacklist.txt in the mod root to exclude them from hacking and boarding.
  • Battle-end backstop - if the enemy has no surviving deployed ships for 10 seconds, the enemy fleet is ordered to retreat so battles always end cleanly.
  • Capture transition - captured targets go through a short paralyzed, phase-like transition (board 10 s / hack 5 s, follows battle speed), then switch to your side; after capture they slowly repair (+0.5% max hull per second, up to 20% total).
  • Post-battle ownership - captured ships join your fleet directly after the battle (captain removed; counted as your kills for bounty settlements).

Detailed mechanics and settingsMod Settings (LunaLib)
Almost every value is adjustable in-game via Mod Settings: hack range/rate, ECM multipliers, size multipliers, boarding hit requirements, malfunction chances and durations, transition times, repair rate, enemy-can-use toggle, custom fighter sprite toggle and more. A linked-slider scheme keeps the settings page compact: only the frigate-tier values are exposed, and the other hull sizes derive automatically.

Compatibility and known issues
  • Made for 0.98a-RC8; not tested against other versions.
  • The mod was developed and tested in a partially Chinese-localized environment; behavior in a full English environment is not yet fully confirmed (feedback welcome).
  • Known limitation: captures completed while the battle stays in fleet-control (strategy) mode the whole time may skip the transition animation (final ownership is unaffected); it recovers after entering combat mode once.
  • Ship hulls added by other mods work as capture targets unless blacklisted.

FAQ
Q
Why does nothing happen when I board?
A
Boarding hits require fighters with CR above 0 to touch the target; install the Boarding Driver Core (0 OP) on at least one of your ships if you want the malfunction effects.
Q
Why is my captured ship missing after battle?
A
Captured ships join your fleet directly after the battle ends; check the Reserve tab of your fleet. Ships still in their transition phase when the battle ends are also handled by the backstop.
Q
Can enemies use this mod against me?
A
By default yes (toggle in Mod Settings, "enemy can use"): enemy Hacking Arrays and Boarding Pods work from the enemy perspective. Turn it off if you do not want enemies to capture your ships.
Q
How do I exclude a ship from capture?
A
Add its hull id to capture_blacklist.txt in the mod root.
Q
Compressed file download was just loose files once unzipped?
A
Create a folder with the same name as the compressed file inside the mods folder, and extract the contents of the compressed file into that folder.

AI use disclaimerSome or all assets and code in this mod were created using AI tools:
  • Code: Doubao (ByteDance's AI assistant) - the entire Java codebase was written by the AI, referencing vanilla Starsector code and the open-source mods listed in Credits below, then tested and iterated in-game.
  • Fighter sprites: Doubao (AI-generated pixel art), with hand-drawn adjustments by the author.
The author is a complete coding novice and this is their first mod; the AI did not use any additional training data beyond its base model. The mod was tested and verified in-game across many iterations before release.
